card.name: Words leading into stopping or failing
card.fires_on: The small word "to" (also "not", "be", "or") right after phrases about inability, failure or dose-stopping triggers, such as "unable to" or "leading to". It appears in dose-modification and discontinuation passages of drug labels.

modes.label: Inability or urge before a verb
modes.description: "to" after unable, inability, impossible or urge, introducing the action that fails or occurs.
modes.example: Permanently discontinue QINLOCK in patients who are unable<< to>> tolerate 100 mg orally once

modes.label: Reactions leading to stopping
modes.description: "to" or a linking word after phrases about reactions leading to dose reduction or discontinuation.
modes.example: Infusion-related reactions leading<< to>> permanent discontinuation of RYBREV

modes.label: Other link words before a stop instruction
modes.description: "not", "be" or "or" before a verb or noun about stopping or an unmet step.
modes.example: If the green light still does<< not>> turn off, discard the inhaler and

card.writes: It seems to steer the next word away from "run/running" senses, with no clear positive direction.
card.plain: It marks the little linking word just before a label says a treatment stops, fails or cannot be continued.
